q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 180 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 84,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him is:
e: Leave salary per day = (Rs 84,000 + 50 per cent DA) / 30 = Rs 1,26,000 / 30 = Rs 4,200; cash equivalent for 180 days = 4,200 x 180 = Rs 7,56,000.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 45,000 per month applies for House Building Advance for construction of a house on his own plot, the estimated cost of construction being Rs 80 lakh. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him is:
e: HBA is limited to the least of 139 times basic pay (139 x Rs 45,000 = Rs 62,55,000), the estimated cost of construction (Rs 80 lakh) and the ceiling of Rs 1 crore; hence Rs 62,55,000.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 70,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account is:
e: Government contribution to NPS Tier-I = 14 per cent of (basic pay + DA) = 14 per cent of (Rs 70,000 + Rs 35,000) = 14 per cent of Rs 1,05,000 = Rs 14,700 per month.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, where a railway servant retires on superannuation with qualifying service of less than 25 years but not less than 10 years, the assured payout admissible to him is:

options.A: 50 per cent of the average basic pay of the last 12 months, in all cases
options.B: Proportionately reduced from the payout admissible for 25 years of qualifying service
options.D: Payable only as a lump sum

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, the full assured payout corresponds to 25 years of qualifying service; for service of less than 25 years but not less than 10 years, the payout is proportionately reduced.

q: The leave salary admissible to a railway servant during a period of Hospital Leave is:

options.A: Equal to the leave salary during Leave on Average Pay for the entire period
options.B: Equal to the leave salary during Leave on Half Average Pay for the entire period
options.C: Nil, as hospital leave carries no leave salary
options.D: Equal to the leave salary during Leave on Average Pay for the first 120 days and equal to the leave salary during Leave on Half Average Pay thereafter

e: During Hospital Leave, leave salary is equal to that during Leave on Average Pay for the first 120 days and equal to that during Leave on Half Average Pay for the period thereafter.

q: Under the Fundamental Rules, an increment in the pay of a railway servant shall ordinarily be drawn as a matter of course, unless it is:

options.A: Withheld by the competent authority as a measure of penalty
options.B: Deferred by the drawing officer for want of funds
options.C: Stopped by the Accounts Office without orders of the competent authority
options.D: Postponed at the request of another railway servant

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, an increment shall ordinarily be drawn as a matter of course unless it is withheld by the competent authority as a measure of penalty.

q: Reservation of 10 per cent for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) on the Railways is applicable:

options.A: In direct recruitment as well as in promotion
options.D: Only in the Limited Departmental Competitive Examination

e: The 10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections applies only in direct recruitment; it is not applicable in promotions.

q: Under Rule 7 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not engage himself in, or participate in, any demonstration which:

options.A: Is held on a public holiday
options.B: Is prejudicial to the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, public order, decency or morality
options.C: Is organised by a recognised trade union for any purpose whatsoever
options.D: Takes place outside the railway premises

e: Rule 7 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 prohibits a railway servant from engaging in or participating in any demonstration prejudicial to the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, public order, decency or morality.

q: Under Section 10 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, where a request for information relates partly to information which is exempt from disclosure, the Central Public Information Officer may:

options.B: Provide the information only after obtaining the orders of the Central Information Commission
options.C: Provide access to the entire record without severing any part
options.D: Provide access to that part of the record which does not contain the exempt information, after severing it from the exempt part

e: Under Section 10 of the RTI Act, 2005, access may be provided to that part of a record which does not contain exempt information, after severing it from the part containing the exempt information.

q: Family pension admissible to the family of a railway servant who dies while in service commences from:

options.A: The day following the date of his death
options.B: The first day of the month following his death
options.C: The date on which the family applies for it
options.D: The date of issue of the Pension Payment Order

e: Family pension admissible to the family of a railway servant who dies while in service commences from the day following the date of his death.

q: The Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) allotted to a subscriber under the National Pension System:

options.A: Changes every time the subscriber is transferred to another office
options.B: Is cancelled and re-allotted on his promotion
options.C: Remains the same throughout and is portable across offices, sectors and locations
options.D: Lapses on the subscriber attaining the age of 60 years

e: The Permanent Retirement Account Number allotted under NPS remains the same throughout and is portable across offices, sectors and locations; it does not change on transfer or promotion.

q: A railway servant on tour is provided with free boarding and free lodging by the Government. The Daily Allowance admissible to him for that day is:

options.B: 25 per cent of the Daily Allowance
options.C: 50 per cent of the Daily Allowance

e: Where a railway servant on tour is provided both free boarding and free lodging, only 25 per cent of the Daily Allowance is admissible for that day.

q: Under Rule 5 of the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, a railway servant may be placed under suspension by the competent authority where:

options.A: He has submitted an application for voluntary retirement
options.B: He has been transferred to another station
options.C: He has proceeded on leave for more than 30 days
options.D: A disciplinary proceeding against him is contemplated or pending, or a case against him in respect of a criminal offence is under investigation, inquiry or trial

e: Under Rule 5 of the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, suspension may be ordered where a disciplinary proceeding is contemplated or pending, or a case in respect of a criminal offence is under investigation, inquiry or trial.

q: The training of Act Apprentices engaged on the Railways is governed by the:
e: The training of Act Apprentices engaged on the Railways is governed by the Apprentices Act, 1961.

q: Before a person is appointed to railway service, he is required to:

options.A: Produce a certificate of having passed the departmental examination
options.B: Undergo a medical examination and be certified fit for railway service by the competent medical authority
options.C: Complete two years of apprenticeship in all cases
options.D: Furnish a security deposit equal to one month's pay

e: Before appointment to railway service, a person is required to undergo a medical examination and be certified fit for railway service by the competent medical authority.

q: A railway pensioner dies on a particular day. The pension for that day is:

options.B: Payable only if the pensioner had completed that month
options.D: Payable to his nominee or legal heir, as pension is payable up to and including the day of death

e: Pension is payable up to and including the day of death, so the pension for the day of death is payable to the pensioner's nominee or legal heir.

q: Casual leave admissible to a railway servant can be availed of:

options.A: In full-day as well as half-day spells
options.D: Only during the first half of the calendar year

e: Casual leave admissible to a railway servant can be availed of in full-day as well as half-day spells.

q: Where an applicant seeks information which relates to, or has been supplied by, a third party and has been treated as confidential by that third party, the Central Public Information Officer shall, under Section 11 of the Right to Information Act, 2005:

options.A: Disclose the information without informing the third party
options.C: Give a written notice to the third party and invite his submissions before deciding on disclosure
options.D: Transfer the application to the third party

e: Under Section 11 of the RTI Act, 2005, where information relates to a third party and has been treated as confidential by it, the CPIO shall give written notice to the third party and invite its submissions before deciding on disclosure.

q: Complimentary passes on the Railways are issued to:

options.A: Only serving railway servants proceeding on leave
options.B: Persons who are not railway servants, in recognition of distinguished or meritorious service, such as gallantry award winners
options.C: Only the family members of retired railway servants
options.D: Only railway servants transferred in public interest

e: Complimentary passes are issued to persons who are not railway servants, in recognition of distinguished or meritorious service, such as gallantry award winners.

q: Service rendered by a railway servant on deputation to an ex-cadre post under the Government is treated, for the purpose of pension in his parent cadre, as:

options.B: Counting only if he is permanently absorbed in the ex-cadre post
options.D: Qualifying service, subject to the prescribed conditions regarding pension contribution

e: Service rendered on deputation to an ex-cadre post counts as qualifying service for pension in the parent cadre, subject to the prescribed conditions regarding pension contribution.

q: In regard to the railway quarter allotted to a railway servant, the correct position is that he:

options.A: Shall not sublet the quarter, or any portion of it, to any person
options.B: May sublet the quarter with the permission of his immediate supervisor
options.C: May sublet the quarter if he is transferred within the same station
options.D: May sublet the quarter after completing ten years of service

e: In regard to the railway quarter allotted to him, a railway servant shall not sublet the quarter, or any portion of it, to any person.

q: The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) has been introduced as an option available to:

options.A: All railway pensioners who retired before 2004
options.B: Only Group 'A' officers of the Railways
options.C: Railway servants who are covered under the National Pension System

e: The Unified Pension Scheme has been introduced as an option available to railway servants who are covered under the National Pension System.

q: The full pension admissible to a retiring railway servant is sanctioned by the competent authority only when:

options.A: He has never availed any leave during his service
options.B: The service rendered by him has been found to be entirely satisfactory
options.C: He has not commuted any portion of his pension
options.D: He surrenders his railway quarter before the date of retirement

e: The full pension admissible to a retiring railway servant is sanctioned only when the service rendered by him has been found to be entirely satisfactory.

q: The class of accommodation admissible to a railway servant on a privilege pass is determined with reference to his:

options.B: Age at the time of travel
options.D: Pay level in the pay matrix

e: The class of accommodation admissible to a railway servant on a privilege pass is determined with reference to his pay level in the pay matrix.

q: Under the provisions relating to nomination for arrears of pension, the arrears of pension remaining unpaid at the time of the death of a railway pensioner are payable to:

options.A: The pension disbursing bank, which retains them
options.B: The Government, as a lapse in every case
options.C: The person nominated by the pensioner for receiving the arrears
options.D: Only the eldest surviving son of the pensioner

e: The arrears of pension remaining unpaid at the time of the death of a pensioner are payable to the person nominated by the pensioner for receiving the arrears of pension.

q: 'Special pay', as defined in the Fundamental Rules applicable to railway servants, means:

options.A: The pay granted to a railway servant for holding additional charge of another post
options.B: The additional pay granted to a railway servant to save him from a loss of substantive pay on account of revision of pay
options.C: The pay drawn by a railway servant in an officiating capacity in a higher post
options.D: An addition, of the nature of pay, to the emoluments of a post or of a railway servant, granted in consideration of the specially arduous nature of the duties or of a specific addition to the work or responsibility

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, special pay is an addition, of the nature of pay, to the emoluments of a post or of a railway servant, granted in consideration of the specially arduous nature of the duties or of a specific addition to the work or responsibility.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 44,900 in Level 6 of the pay matrix is promoted to a post in Level 7. On fixation of his pay, one increment is first granted in Level 6, taking his pay to the next cell of Rs 46,200, and his pay is then fixed in Level 7 at the cell equal to, or next above, that amount. His basic pay in Level 7 will be:
e: On promotion, one increment is first granted in Level 6 (Rs 44,900 to Rs 46,200) and the pay is then fixed in Level 7 at the cell equal to that amount, i.e. Rs 46,200.

q: The pay and allowances of railway servants for a month are ordinarily disbursed on:

options.A: The last working day of the same month
options.B: The first working day of the next month
options.C: The seventh day of the next month
options.D: The last working day of the next month

e: The pay and allowances of railway servants for a month are ordinarily disbursed on the last working day of the same month.

q: 'Foreign service', in relation to a railway servant, means service:

options.B: Rendered under a foreign employer within India
options.C: Rendered on deputation to another department of the same Railway
options.D: In which he receives his pay, with the sanction of the Government, from a source other than the revenues of the Government or the Railways

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, foreign service means service in which the railway servant receives his pay, with the sanction of the Government, from a source other than the revenues of the Government or the Railways.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after completing full qualifying service. His average emoluments are Rs 76,000 per month. The amount of his monthly pension will be:
e: Pension = 50 per cent of average emoluments = 50 per cent of Rs 76,000 = Rs 38,000 per month.

q: Invalid pension is granted to a railway servant who retires from service on account of bodily or mental infirmity which permanently incapacitates him for service. The grant of invalid pension requires:

options.A: A declaration by the railway servant himself that he is unfit for service
options.B: A certificate from any registered medical practitioner
options.C: Completion of at least twenty years of qualifying service
options.D: A medical certificate from the competent medical authority certifying his permanent incapacity

e: Invalid pension requires a medical certificate from the competent medical authority certifying that the railway servant is permanently incapacitated for service by bodily or mental infirmity.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 80,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate will be:
e: Family pension at the enhanced rate = 50 per cent of last basic pay = 50 per cent of Rs 80,000 = Rs 40,000 per month.

q: Commutation of pension for a lump sum payment is NOT admissible in the case of:
e: Commutation of pension for a lump sum payment is not admissible in the case of family pension, which is payable to the family and not to the employee himself.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 25,000. He commutes 40 per cent of his pension. Taking the commutation value for his age on the next birthday as 8.194 for each rupee of annual pension commuted, the lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Pension commuted per month = 40 per cent of Rs 25,000 = Rs 10,000; annual amount = Rs 1,20,000; lump sum = 1,20,000 x 8.194 = Rs 9,83,280.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Additional quantum of pension is also admissible to a family pensioner on his or her attaining the age of 80 years.
2. The additional quantum in the case of a family pensioner is calculated on the enhanced rate of family pension, wherever the enhanced rate is payable.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 only is correct: additional quantum of pension is admissible to a family pensioner on attaining the age of 80 years. Statement 2 is wrong because the additional quantum is calculated on the normal rate of family pension, not on the enhanced rate.

q: A railway pensioner, whose basic pension is Rs 45,000 per month, attains the age of 85 years. The additional quantum of pension admissible to him will be:
e: On attaining the age of 85 years, the additional quantum of pension is 30 per cent of the basic pension = 30 per cent of Rs 45,000 = Rs 13,500 per month.

q: The retirement gratuity payable to a railway servant, calculated at one-fourth of his emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, shall not exceed:
e: Retirement gratuity at one-fourth of emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service is subject to a maximum of 16.5 times the emoluments.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 30 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 92,000 per month. The retirement gratuity admissible to him will be:
e: Retirement gratuity = 1/4 of emoluments x completed six-monthly periods = Rs 23,000 x 60 (30 years) = Rs 13,80,000.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 1,20,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate will be:
e: Family pension at the normal rate = 30 per cent of last basic pay = 30 per cent of Rs 1,20,000 = Rs 36,000 per month.

q: Pension Adalats organised on the Railways are intended for:

options.A: On-the-spot redressal of the grievances of pensioners and family pensioners
options.B: Revision of the pension of pensioners who retired before 01.01.2016
options.D: Audit of pension payments made by banks

e: Pension Adalats organised on the Railways are intended for on-the-spot redressal of the grievances of pensioners and family pensioners.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The pension of a railway pensioner who retired before 01.01.2016 can be revised by notional fixation of his pay in the pay matrix of the 7th CPC.
2. Under this method, the pension is arrived at as 50 per cent of the notional pay so fixed, and the pensioner is allowed the benefit of whichever of the prescribed methods is more advantageous to him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the pension of a pre-2016 pensioner can be revised by notional fixation of pay in the 7th CPC pay matrix, with pension at 50 per cent of the notional pay, and the benefit of whichever prescribed method is more advantageous is allowed.

q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, a subscriber retiring on superannuation is entitled, in addition to the assured payout, to a lump sum payment equal to:

options.A: 60 per cent of his individual corpus
options.B: One month's pay for every completed year of service
options.C: One-twelfth of his annual pay at retirement
options.D: One-tenth of his last drawn basic pay plus dearness allowance, for every completed six-monthly period of qualifying service

e: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, a subscriber retiring on superannuation is entitled, in addition to the assured payout, to a lump sum equal to one-tenth of his last drawn basic pay plus dearness allowance for every completed six-monthly period of qualifying service.

q: In regard to subscription to the General Provident Fund by a railway servant who is due to retire on superannuation, the correct position is that:

options.A: He may discontinue his subscription during the last three months of service before the date of retirement
options.B: He must continue his subscription till the date of his retirement
options.C: His subscription is automatically enhanced during the last three months of service
options.D: He may withdraw his entire balance three months before retirement without any condition

e: A railway servant due to retire on superannuation may discontinue his subscription to the General Provident Fund during the last three months of service before the date of retirement.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 55,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account will be:
e: Government contribution to NPS Tier-I = 14 per cent of (basic pay + DA) = 14 per cent of (Rs 55,000 + Rs 27,500) = 14 per cent of Rs 82,500 = Rs 11,550 per month.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 52,000 per month applies for House Building Advance for construction of a house, the estimated cost of construction being Rs 90 lakh. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him will be:
e: HBA is limited to the least of 139 times basic pay (139 x Rs 52,000 = Rs 72,28,000), the estimated cost of construction (Rs 90 lakh) and the ceiling of Rs 1 crore; hence Rs 72,28,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The advance for the purchase of a motor car (Motor Car Advance) stands abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation.
2. Personal Computer Advance continues to be admissible to railway servants as an interest-bearing advance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Motor Car Advance stands abolished under the 7th CPC dispensation, while the Personal Computer Advance continues to be admissible as an interest-bearing advance.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 210 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 64,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary admissible to him will be:
e: Leave salary per day = (Rs 64,000 + 50 per cent DA) / 30 = Rs 96,000 / 30 = Rs 3,200; cash equivalent for 210 days = 3,200 x 210 = Rs 6,72,000.

q: Which of the following statements regarding combination of leave is correct?

options.A: Leave on Average Pay cannot be combined with any other kind of leave
options.B: Leave on Average Pay can be combined only with casual leave
options.C: Leave on Average Pay can be combined only with restricted holidays
options.D: Leave on Average Pay may be combined with leave on half average pay, commuted leave and extraordinary leave

e: Leave on Average Pay may be combined with leave on half average pay, commuted leave and extraordinary leave; it is casual leave and restricted holidays that generally cannot be combined with regular leave.

q: The standard of distant vision prescribed for the 'Aye-One' (A-1) medical category on the Railways is:
e: The standard of distant vision prescribed for the Aye-One (A-1) medical category is 6/6, 6/6 without glasses.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, no adult worker shall be required to work for a period of more than five hours in a factory before he has had an interval for rest of at least:
e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, no adult worker shall be required to work for more than five hours in a factory before he has had an interval for rest of at least thirty minutes.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker does not avail of the whole of the leave with wages admissible to him in a year, the unavailed leave may be carried forward to the succeeding year, provided that the total amount of leave so carried forward shall not exceed:
e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, unavailed leave with wages may be carried forward to the succeeding year, provided the total leave so carried forward does not exceed 30 days.

q: In accordance with the instructions of the Government on the creation and continuation of posts, a post which has remained vacant for a period of more than five years is:
e: In accordance with Government instructions on creation and continuation of posts, a post which has remained vacant for a period of more than five years is deemed to have been abolished.

q: Creation of a new post on a zonal Railway requires, before it is sanctioned:

options.A: Approval of the Railway Board in every case
options.B: Sanction of the General Manager alone
options.C: Recommendation of the head of the department concerned only
options.D: The prior concurrence of the associated finance, that is, the Principal Financial Adviser

e: Creation of a new post on a zonal Railway requires, before it is sanctioned, the prior concurrence of the associated finance, that is, the Principal Financial Adviser.

q: Recruitment to non-gazetted Group 'C' posts on the Railways is conducted through:
e: Recruitment to non-gazetted Group C posts on the Railways is conducted through the Railway Recruitment Boards.

q: In direct recruitment on the Railways, the relaxation admissible in the upper age limit is:

options.A: 3 years for Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and 5 years for Other Backward Classes
options.B: 5 years for Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and 3 years for Other Backward Classes
options.C: 5 years for both Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes
options.D: 3 years for both Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes

e: In direct recruitment on the Railways, the relaxation in the upper age limit is five years for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and three years for Other Backward Classes.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appointments on compassionate grounds on the Railways are limited to 5 per cent of the vacancies falling under the direct recruitment quota.
2. Such appointments are normally considered only where the request is made within five years of the death of the railway servant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: appointments on compassionate grounds are limited to 5 per cent of the vacancies under the direct recruitment quota, and such appointments are normally considered only where the request is made within five years of the death of the railway servant.

q: A casual labourer with temporary status is absorbed in a regular post on the Railways. For the purpose of pension, the period of service rendered by him in temporary status is counted as qualifying service to the extent of:
e: On absorption of a casual labourer with temporary status in a regular post, 50 per cent of the period of service rendered in temporary status is counted as qualifying service for pension.

q: Substitutes on the Railways are:

options.A: Apprentices engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961
options.B: Casual labour engaged for seasonal work
options.C: Staff engaged on daily wages for a specific work of short duration
options.D: Persons engaged in railway service in place of regular employees who are absent on leave or otherwise

e: Substitutes on the Railways are persons engaged in railway service in place of regular employees who are absent on leave or otherwise.

q: A railway servant who tenders technical resignation and joins a new post under the Government retains his lien on the post held by him in the parent cadre for a period of:
e: A railway servant who tenders technical resignation and joins a new post under the Government retains his lien on the post held in the parent cadre for a period of two years.

q: The Permanent Negotiating Machinery (PNM) on the Railways functions at:

options.C: Three levels — Division, Zonal Railway and Railway Board

e: The Permanent Negotiating Machinery (PNM) on the Railways functions at three levels - Division, Zonal Railway and Railway Board.

q: The engagement of a person as an Act Apprentice on the Railways:

options.A: Entitles him to absorption in railway service on completion of his training
options.B: Does not confer on him any right to employment in the Railways
options.C: Makes him a railway servant during the period of his training
options.D: Guarantees him preference, as a matter of right, in all railway recruitments

e: The engagement of a person as an Act Apprentice is only for training and does not confer on him any right to employment in the Railways.

q: Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities and for ex-servicemen in direct recruitment is described as 'horizontal reservation' because it:

options.A: Is provided separately within the quota of each reserved category
options.C: Cuts across the vertical categories of reservation, namely Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and the unreserved category
options.D: Can be interchanged with vertical reservation at the discretion of the recruiting authority

e: Reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities and for ex-servicemen is called horizontal reservation because it cuts across the vertical categories of reservation - Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and the unreserved category.

q: 'Cadre', as defined in the Fundamental Rules applicable to railway servants, means:

options.A: The seniority list of a service
options.B: The strength of a service, or a part of a service, sanctioned as a separate unit
options.C: The total number of employees working in an office at a given time
options.D: A group of officers recruited to a service in the same year

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, cadre means the strength of a service, or a part of a service, sanctioned as a separate unit.

q: Rule 12 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, relating to subscriptions and raising of funds, provides that a railway servant shall not, without the previous sanction of the competent authority:

options.A: Ask for, or accept, contributions to, or otherwise associate himself with the raising of, any funds or other collections in pursuance of any object whatsoever
options.B: Contribute to the Staff Benefit Fund through his pay bill
options.C: Subscribe to the General Provident Fund
options.D: Donate blood at a blood donation camp

e: Rule 12 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 provides that a railway servant shall not, without the previous sanction of the competent authority, ask for or accept contributions to, or otherwise associate himself with, the raising of any funds or collections for any object.

q: In the matter of lending and borrowing of money, the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 provide that a railway servant shall not:

options.A: Invest his savings in Government securities
options.B: Hold a savings account in a nationalised bank
options.C: Make occasional investments through a recognised stock broker
options.D: Lend money at interest to, or borrow money from, a person with whom he has, or is likely to have, official dealings

e: Under the Conduct Rules, a railway servant shall not lend money at interest to, or borrow money from, a person with whom he has, or is likely to have, official dealings.

q: On his first appointment to railway service, a railway servant is required to make and subscribe an oath, or affirmation, of:

options.C: Allegiance to the Constitution of India

e: On his first appointment to railway service, a railway servant is required to make and subscribe an oath, or affirmation, of allegiance to the Constitution of India.

q: Under Section 8(1)(i) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, Cabinet papers, including records of deliberations of the Council of Ministers, are exempt from disclosure:

options.B: Until the decision has been taken and the matter is complete or over
options.C: For a fixed period of ten years

e: Under Section 8(1)(i) of the RTI Act, 2005, Cabinet papers, including records of deliberations of the Council of Ministers, are exempt from disclosure until the decision has been taken and the matter is complete or over.

q: The number of sets of privilege passes admissible in a calendar year to a Group 'A' or Group 'B' gazetted railway officer is:
e: The number of sets of privilege passes admissible in a calendar year to a Group A or Group B gazetted railway officer is six sets.

q: In direct recruitment to Level-1 (erstwhile Group 'D') posts on the Railways, the percentage of vacancies reserved for ex-servicemen is:
e: In direct recruitment to Level-1 posts on the Railways, 20 per cent of the vacancies are reserved for ex-servicemen.

q: The joining time admissible to a railway servant on transfer in public interest, including any extension that may be granted by the competent authority in special circumstances, shall not exceed:
e: The joining time admissible to a railway servant on transfer in public interest, including any extension granted by the competent authority in special circumstances, shall not exceed 30 days.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after completing full qualifying service. His average emoluments are Rs 58,000 per month. The amount of his monthly pension will be:
e: Pension = 50 per cent of average emoluments = 50 per cent of Rs 58,000 = Rs 29,000 per month.

q: Under the Fundamental Rules applicable to railway servants, a 'compensatory allowance' means:

options.A: A fee paid to a railway servant for performing work of an occasional or intermittent character
options.B: The pay drawn by a railway servant in respect of a post held by him in an officiating capacity
options.C: An allowance granted to a railway servant who is required to perform duty on a holiday
options.D: An allowance granted to meet personal expenditure necessitated by the special circumstances in which duty is performed

e: Under the Fundamental Rules, a compensatory allowance means an allowance granted to meet personal expenditure necessitated by the special circumstances in which duty is performed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Leave on Half Average Pay is admissible to a railway servant on medical certificate as well as on private affairs.
2. Leave Not Due can be granted to a temporary railway servant who has no Leave on Half Average Pay at his credit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 only is correct: Leave on Half Average Pay is admissible on medical certificate and on private affairs. Statement 2 is wrong because Leave Not Due is not admissible to a temporary servant; it is granted only against half-pay leave to be earned in future.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 13 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 52,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family is:
e: Death gratuity = 20 times the emoluments = 20 x Rs 52,000 = Rs 10,40,000.

q: Rule 3(2) of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 casts a specific responsibility on every railway servant holding a supervisory post. The responsibility is to:

options.A: Take all possible steps to ensure the integrity and devotion to duty of all railway servants for the time being under his control and authority
options.B: Submit the Annual Immovable Property Returns of his subordinates to the Government
options.C: Hold a departmental inquiry against any subordinate found wanting in devotion to duty
options.D: Report every case of misconduct of a subordinate directly to the Central Vigilance Commission

e: Rule 3(2) of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 requires every railway servant holding a supervisory post to take all possible steps to ensure the integrity and devotion to duty of all railway servants under his control and authority.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Family pension is admissible to the legally wedded spouse of a deceased railway pensioner even where the marriage took place after the retirement of the pensioner.
2. A child born to a railway pensioner after his retirement is eligible for family pension on the death of the pensioner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: family pension is admissible to the legally wedded spouse even where the marriage took place after the pensioner's retirement, and a child born to a pensioner after his retirement is also eligible for family pension on the pensioner's death.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 270 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 60,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him is:
e: Leave salary per day = (Rs 60,000 + 50 per cent DA) / 30 = Rs 90,000 / 30 = Rs 3,000; cash equivalent for 270 days = 3,000 x 270 = Rs 8,10,000.

q: In regard to the nomination made by a railway servant for Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity, the correct position is that:

options.A: The nomination, once made, cannot be altered under any circumstances
options.B: The nomination can be modified by the railway servant at any time before the gratuity is paid
options.C: The nomination can be modified only with the permission of the pension sanctioning authority, and that too after retirement
options.D: The nomination lapses automatically on the marriage of the railway servant

e: The nomination for Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity can be modified by the railway servant at any time before the gratuity is paid; it is not irrevocable once made.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Assured Career Progression (ACP) scheme, two financial upgradations were admissible to a railway servant on completion of 12 years and 24 years of regular service.
2. The Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) scheme, which replaced the ACP scheme, came into effect from 1st September, 2008.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: under the ACP scheme, two financial upgradations were admissible on completion of 12 years and 24 years of regular service, and the MACP scheme which replaced it came into effect from 1st September, 2008.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 38,100 in Level 5 of the pay matrix is promoted to a post in Level 6. One increment is first granted to him in Level 5, taking his pay to the next cell, and his pay is then fixed in Level 6 at the cell equal to, or next above, that amount. His basic pay in Level 6 will be:
e: On promotion, one increment in Level 5 takes the pay from Rs 38,100 to Rs 39,300, and the pay is then fixed in Level 6 at the cell next above that amount, i.e. Rs 39,900.

q: Under Rule 14 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not, except with the previous sanction of the Government:

options.A: Receive any complimentary address or accept any testimonial, or attend any meeting or entertainment held in his honour
options.B: Attend the marriage ceremony of a subordinate railway servant
options.C: Participate in a meeting of a recognised trade union of railway servants
options.D: Accept an invitation to a social function from a fellow railway servant

e: Under Rule 14 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not, except with the previous sanction of the Government, receive any complimentary address or accept any testimonial, or attend any meeting or entertainment held in his honour.

q: A railway pensioner's monthly pension is Rs 50,000. He commutes 40 per cent of his pension. Taking the commutation value for his age on the next birthday as 8.194 for each rupee of annual pension commuted, the lump sum commuted value payable to him will be:
e: Pension commuted per month = 40 per cent of Rs 50,000 = Rs 20,000; annual amount = Rs 2,40,000; lump sum = 2,40,000 x 8.194 = Rs 19,66,560.

q: In regard to the pension and gratuity payable to a retired railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: The pension can be assigned by the pensioner in favour of a member of his family
options.B: No pension or gratuity is liable to seizure or attachment in execution of a decree of a court
options.C: The gratuity can be attached by a court towards satisfaction of a money decree against the pensioner
options.D: The pension can be attached to the extent of one-half in execution of a maintenance decree

e: No pension or gratuity payable to a retired railway servant is liable to seizure or attachment in execution of a decree of a court, nor can the pension be assigned by the pensioner.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The appellate authority under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules can impose on a railway servant a penalty which the disciplinary authority was itself not competent to impose.
2. The appellate authority may confirm, enhance, reduce or set aside the penalty imposed by the disciplinary authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 2 only is correct: the appellate authority may confirm, enhance, reduce or set aside the penalty imposed. Statement 1 is wrong because the appellate authority cannot impose a penalty which the disciplinary authority itself was not competent to impose.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 40,000 per month applies for House Building Advance for the purchase of a ready-built house costing Rs 50 lakh. The maximum amount of advance admissible to him is:
e: HBA for purchase of a ready-built house is limited to the least of the cost of the house (Rs 50 lakh), 139 times basic pay (139 x Rs 40,000 = Rs 55,60,000) and the ceiling of Rs 1 crore; hence Rs 50,00,000.

q: Under Rule 6 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not join, or continue to be a member of, an association:

options.A: Which is not registered as a trade union
options.B: Which does not restrict its membership to railway servants only
options.C: Which has not been recognised by the Railway Administration
options.D: The objects or activities of which are prejudicial to the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, public order or morality

e: Under Rule 6 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, a railway servant shall not join or continue to be a member of an association whose objects or activities are prejudicial to the sovereignty and integrity of India, public order or morality.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 96,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate will be:
e: Family pension at the enhanced rate = 50 per cent of last basic pay = 50 per cent of Rs 96,000 = Rs 48,000 per month.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Service as a probationer is treated as 'duty' for the purposes of the Fundamental Rules.
2. The entire period spent by a railway servant under suspension is treated as 'duty' for all purposes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 only is correct: service as a probationer is treated as duty for the purposes of the Fundamental Rules. Statement 2 is wrong because a period of suspension is treated as duty only to the extent ordered by the competent authority, not for all purposes.

q: A railway servant who is due to retire on superannuation may make a final (non-refundable) withdrawal from the balance at his credit in the General Provident Fund, without assigning any reason, during the period of twelve months before the date of his retirement, up to:

options.A: 50 per cent of the balance at his credit
options.B: 75 per cent of the balance at his credit
options.C: Two-thirds of the balance at his credit
options.D: 90 per cent of the balance at his credit

e: A railway servant due to retire on superannuation may make a final (non-refundable) withdrawal from the General Provident Fund, without assigning any reason, during the twelve months before retirement, up to 90 per cent of the balance at his credit.

q: Project casual labour engaged on the Railways is granted temporary status on completion of continuous service of:
e: Project casual labour engaged on the Railways is granted temporary status on completion of 180 days of continuous service.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 70,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate will be:
e: Family pension at the normal rate = 30 per cent of last basic pay = 30 per cent of Rs 70,000 = Rs 21,000 per month.

q: A railway servant who marries, or enters into a marriage with, a person having a nationality other than Indian is required to:

options.A: Obtain the prior permission of the Government for the marriage
options.B: Resign from railway service before such marriage
options.C: Report the marriage to the prescribed authority within a period of one year
options.D: Intimate the fact to the Government forthwith

e: A railway servant who marries, or enters into a marriage with, a person having a nationality other than Indian is required to intimate the fact to the Government forthwith.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 26 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 74,000 per month. The retirement gratuity admissible to him is:
e: Retirement gratuity = 1/4 of emoluments x completed six-monthly periods = Rs 18,500 x 52 (26 years) = Rs 9,62,000.

q: A railway pensioner had commuted a portion of his pension and the commuted portion has since been restored to him on completion of fifteen years. In regard to a further commutation of his pension, the correct position is that:

options.A: He may commute up to 40 per cent of the restored pension
options.B: He may commute a further portion with the sanction of the Railway Board
options.C: He is not entitled to commute any portion of his pension again
options.D: He may commute up to 20 per cent of his pension after a fresh medical examination

e: Once the commuted portion of pension has been restored after completion of fifteen years, the pensioner is not entitled to commute any portion of his pension again.

q: Substitutes engaged on the open line on the Railways attain temporary status on completion of:
e: Substitutes engaged on the open line on the Railways attain temporary status on completion of 120 days of continuous service.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 80,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account will be:
e: Government contribution to NPS Tier-I = 14 per cent of (basic pay + DA) = 14 per cent of (Rs 80,000 + Rs 40,000) = 14 per cent of Rs 1,20,000 = Rs 16,800 per month.

q: Promotion of a railway servant to a skilled artisan grade on the Railways is subject to:

options.A: His completing a prescribed course of training in a railway training school
options.B: The recommendation of a selection board constituted for the purpose
options.C: His passing the prescribed trade test
options.D: His rendering a minimum of ten years of service in the unskilled grade

e: Promotion of a railway servant to a skilled artisan grade on the Railways is subject to his passing the prescribed trade test.

q: Where the payment of Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity to a retired railway servant is delayed beyond the prescribed period for reasons not attributable to the railway servant, he becomes entitled to:

options.A: An ex-gratia payment equal to ten per cent of the amount of gratuity
options.B: Interest on the amount of gratuity for the period of delay
options.C: Restoration of the full pension for the period of delay
options.D: A second advance of gratuity pending final payment

e: Where payment of Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity is delayed beyond the prescribed period for reasons not attributable to the railway servant, he is entitled to interest on the amount of gratuity for the period of delay.

q: The services of a railway servant who is still on probation may be terminated for unsatisfactory performance or on the ground of his unsuitability for the post:

options.A: Without invoking the procedure prescribed in the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules
options.B: Only after holding a departmental inquiry under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules
options.C: Only with the prior approval of the Railway Board
options.D: Only after giving him an opportunity to improve during a further period of two years

e: The services of a railway servant who is still on probation may be terminated for unsatisfactory performance or unsuitability for the post without invoking the procedure prescribed in the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules.

q: Candidates belonging to the reserved categories who get selected on their own merit, without availing of any relaxation or concession, are, for the purpose of filling up the vacancies:

options.A: Adjusted against the vacancies reserved for their respective categories
options.B: Treated as unreserved candidates for all future selections also
options.C: Required to give an undertaking that they will not claim reservation in future
options.D: Adjusted against unreserved vacancies and not against the reserved quota

e: Candidates of reserved categories who are selected on their own merit, without availing of any relaxation or concession, are adjusted against unreserved vacancies and not against the vacancies reserved for their respective categories.
